title: Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL, while comments, favorites and follows cascade.
content:
articles.author_id is a nullable foreign key with ondelete SET NULL. The commentaries, favorites and followers_to_followings foreign keys to users use ondelete CASCADE instead.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

title: Article listing defaults to 20 items with a minimum limit of 1 and no maximum.
content:
ArticlesFilters declares limit with default DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT (20) and ge=1, and offset with ge=0. No upper bound is set, so a client can request any page size.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:42

title: articlesCount in list responses is the length of the returned page, not the total number of matching articles.
content:
list_articles sets articles_count to len(articles), the rows returned after limit and offset. No separate count query is run.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:49

title: Invalid tokens and tokens for unknown users are rejected with 403 Forbidden and the same MALFORMED_PAYLOAD message.
content:
_get_current_user maps a token decode error and a missing user to the same HTTPException with status 403 and detail MALFORMED_PAYLOAD. A bad header prefix is also 403, not 401.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:90

title: Only an article's author may update or delete it, checked by comparing usernames.
content:
check_user_can_modify_article returns true only when the article author's username equals the current user's username. There is no admin or role override.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
content:
security.py builds a CryptContext with schemes ["bcrypt"] and deprecated="auto", and both hashing and verification go through it. Changing the scheme list changes which stored hashes can be verified.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

title: All API models expose camelCase JSON field names generated from snake_case attributes.
content:
RWModel sets alias_generator to convert_field_to_camel_case and allows population by field name. Renaming a Python attribute therefore renames the JSON field.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

title: JWT access tokens are signed and verified with the symmetric HS256 algorithm.
content:
The JWT service sets a module constant ALGORITHM to HS256 and uses it both to encode tokens and as the only accepted algorithm when decoding. Signing uses the app secret_key, so the same secret both issues and verifies tokens.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

title: Access tokens expire one week after issue and there is no refresh token.
content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7, and create_access_token_for_user passes it as the expiry delta. No refresh or revocation mechanism exists in the service.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

title: The JWT payload identifies the user by username, not by numeric id.
content:
create_access_token_for_user puts only JWTUser(username=...) into the token, and the current-user dependency loads the user with get_user_by_username. Renaming a user therefore invalidates existing tokens for that user.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

title: Login returns one identical 400 error for an unknown email and for a wrong password.
content:
The login route builds a single wrong_login_error with INCORRECT_LOGIN_INPUT and raises it both when the email is not found and when check_password fails. Callers cannot tell which part was wrong.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:28

title: Database access uses raw SQL files loaded by aiosql over asyncpg, not an ORM.
content:
queries.py loads every .sql file in the sql folder with aiosql using the asyncpg adapter. Repositories call these named queries, and only the dynamic article filter builds SQL with pypika.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

title: An article's slug is derived only from its title with python-slugify, and duplicate titles are rejected.
content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title) with no suffix or id. On create, the route checks whether that slug exists and returns 400 ARTICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS, and the slug column is UNIQUE.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19

title: Changing an article's title regenerates its slug, so the article URL changes.
content:
The update route recomputes the slug from the new title when a title is given and passes it to update_article. Unlike create, the route does not check that the new slug is free, so a collision falls to the UNIQUE constraint.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:100

title: A separate per-user salt is stored in the users table and prepended to the password before bcrypt hashing.
content:
change_password generates a salt with bcrypt.gensalt, stores it on the user, and hashes salt + password. check_password must prepend the same stored salt, so the salt column cannot be dropped or changed without breaking logins.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

title: The Authorization header must use the prefix "Token", not "Bearer".
content:
AppSettings sets jwt_token_prefix to "Token". The auth dependency splits the header on a single space and rejects any other prefix with 403 WRONG_TOKEN_PREFIX.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

title: updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL BEFORE UPDATE trigger, not by application code.
content:
The main migration creates the plpgsql function update_updated_at_column, which sets NEW.updated_at = now(), and attaches it to users, articles and commentaries. Application updates rely on the database to refresh the timestamp.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27
